consequence_for_claims: The first-layer candidate is the window nearest in this terrain-only metric among the 71 eligible windows of the slice search, not a morphological analog of Connecting Ridge. Cards and the paper must not describe it as similar terrain beyond the stated distances; Mode C claim limits apply.
inspected: Viewed both 5 km windows on the 90 m analysis grid as elevation maps with contours (rendered from the D29-resampled DEM caches listed under uncommitted_artifacts_opened), and compared their T3 nu(L) curves and Hurst exponents from data/processed/windows/{moon,earth}.json and the committed candidate table.

numbers_source.relief_ranges: min and max of elevation_m in the two dem_windows caches

observed_discrepancy: The target is one broad massif: about 780 m of relief in a single dome-shaped ridge whose nu grows steadily from 43.4 m at 270 m to 148.2 m at 1080 m (relief H 0.89). The candidate is a mostly flat plain at about 750 to 800 m crossed by a few narrow ridges (up to about 960 m) and a trough (down to about 660 m), about 300 m of relief. Its nu is close to the target at short lags (32.2 m at 270 m) but flattens with lag (54.6 m at 1080 m, relief H 0.38). The RMS log nu distance does not read H, so a window whose roughness saturates beyond a few hundred metres ranks first against a target whose roughness keeps growing with scale. The rank is stable under the clones because the clones move the target's nu by about 0.07%, far less than the factor of 2.7 difference at 1080 m; the stability says nothing about morphological similarity.
record_type: terraluna G4 inspected counterexample (analyst inspection, not generated)
why_this_candidate: It is the only window in the first Pareto layer over terrain_relief and terrain_texture (analysis/g4_candidates.json), and it stays there in 100 of 100 PGDA78 clone runs, so it is the candidate most likely to be read as 'the match'.
